author: reek
body: Every leaf below is call-free by the gate's own analysis: bit-and, bit-or, bit-xor, bit-shl and bit-shru are on a64-is-known-inline, so a64-body-has-non-tail-call answers False for these bodies. But the ARM64 runtime records functions NAMED bit-and, bit-or, bit-xor, bit-shl and bit-shru (Arm64Runtime.codex, a64-record-func), and a64-emit-direct-call prefers a recorded function over the inline arm for any known builtin, so each of these "inline" operations is in fact emitted as a BL to the two-instruction runtime helper. Framed, that BL is harmless. Frameless there is no saved LR, so the first BL destroys x30 and the leaf's RET can never leave the function again.

author: reek
body: Under the current gate (a64-can-be-frameless requires a64-should-tco) all five leaves are emitted FRAMED and this probe passes. Under the reverted widened gate (plain call-free leaves admitted) flp-add32, flp-rotl32 and flp-gmul2 go frameless with a BL inside; flp-plusk goes frameless with a BL to the zero-arg constant flp-mask (the bare IrName arm of a64-emit-name is also a call the analysis cannot see). flp-block is the control: a pure compare-and-literal chain with no bit ops and no named constants, deep enough to walk the frameless local file into x19 if the nested-if result locals overflow.
